Controlled evaluation · Perception

Human-like attention?

A psychophysical comparison of visual search in humans and multimodal large language models.

PaperCodeStudy website

Design

Nine conditions vary feature versus conjunction search, distractor heterogeneity, and 2D versus 3D presentation. The study recruited 1,250 people and retained 157,042 human trials for analysis. Three MLLMs were evaluated on 6,300 synthetic images.

Finding

Across 18 condition summaries, model error rates correlated with human response times (Spearman ρ = 0.91) and human error rates (ρ = 0.82). Yet difficult conjunction scenes produced strongly biased model responses. Humans instead showed changes in response time and accuracy.

Interpretation: agreement in difficulty rankings can coexist with different failure patterns. The results support behavioural diagnosis; they do not, by themselves, identify the models’ internal mechanisms.

Connection to robotics

A human supervisor may assume that a model sees a scene as they do. Testing specific combinations of visual features helps expose where that assumption breaks down. Transfer from these synthetic scenes to real robot perception remains a research question.
